full_judgment: 10. On going to the materials on record it transpires that on 3-7-1992 at 10-30 PM the accused being armed with deadly weapons exploded cocktail inside the mills and also caused mischief to the building premises. Thereby they committed two distinct offences. Of which one is under the Explosive Substances Act and another is under the Penal Code. In revision, two fold grounds were taken to impeach the impugned order. Firstly, the FIR and charge sheet do not disclose any offence against the petitioners. Secondly, over the selfsame occurrence institution of two cases is barred by law. To address the same we hold that the FIR charge sheets and other materials on record clearly discloses the offences under Act. The offences punishable under the Act are the Schedule offences of the Special Powers Act, 1974 which are triable by the Special Tribunal, and other offences are triable by the Ordinary Courts having jurisdiction. It is well settled that Special Tribunals set up under the Special Powers Act are to try only those offences which are mentioned in the schedule to the Act and none other. Moreso, joinder of schedule and non schedule offences is an illegality. So the classes of offences should be tried by two different Courts. Therefore, there is no illegality in continuing the two cases simultaneously by the two different Courts. In view of such facts, we hold that the Tribunal by framing charge tinder sections 3, 4 of the Act, against the petitioners and others committed no illegality. Thus the Rule having no merit fails.
